title: Deploy Python Web Apps in Containers

scenes.line1: How do you deploy Python web apps?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how to deploy your FastAPI, Django, or Flask app so it runs reliably everywhere? Why are containers the go-to solution?

scenes.label: Docker
scenes.sub: Docker gives you a consistent setup, so your app runs the same on any machine or cloud.
scenes.say: Docker makes your environment predictable. No more 'works on my machine' headaches—your app runs the same in development and production.

rows.b: Use Gunicorn for WSGI, Uvicorn for ASGI
Launch app in a managed environment

scenes.say: First, create a Dockerfile for your app. Use multi-stage builds to keep images lean. Pick Gunicorn for synchronous apps or Uvicorn for async ones. Then, run your container wherever you need.

scenes.title: Sample Dockerfile
scenes.say: Here's a typical Dockerfile for a Django app. It installs dependencies and launches your app with Gunicorn, a production-ready server.

scenes.question: Should you use Flask's built-in server in production?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it's good enough for production.
scenes.right: No, use Gunicorn or Uvicorn for production. Built-in servers are only for development.
scenes.say: Don't use Flask's built-in server in production. Always choose Gunicorn or Uvicorn for reliability and performance.
